My worksheet includes a very large number of these data columns. In addition, I'd like to understand the logic of the formula for totaling the quantities needed for various raw parts under completed parts listed across the top of row 1 and also account for the quantities of raw parts that are shipping to other facilities listed in cells B2:K2, the total of which is easy to calculate and displayed in cell L2. Combining the totals in cells L2 and M2 should give me the total amount of raw parts needed both for shipping and building completed parts at this location.

B2:K2 also contains how many raw parts are shipping for other facilities to make their own completed parts, aside from what will be needed to build completed parts here at this one. from pathlib import Path

output_path = Path("/mnt/data/outputs/50682_0_3cdac666/1_50682_output.xlsx")
output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

sheet_name = "PART LIST (2)"
answer_cell = "M2"

wb = load_workbook(input_path, data_only=False)
ws = wb[sheet_name]

# Locate the columns to scan.
# Per the worksheet layout, raw part/quantity pairs start at column O; the quantity is in the cell directly to the right.
start_col = 15  # O

# Derive the last row and column from actual content, rather than assuming preview dimensions.
last_row = 1
last_col = start_col
for row in ws.iter_rows():
    for cell in row:
        if cell.value is not None:
            if cell.row > last_row:
                last_row = cell.row
            if cell.column > last_col:
                last_col = cell.column

# The comparison range must stop one column before the final quantity column,
# because each matched part number contributes the value from the cell immediately to its right.
part_start_col = start_col
part_end_col = max(start_col, last_col - 1)
qty_start_col = part_start_col + 1
qty_end_col = part_end_col + 1

part_range = f"${get_column_letter(part_start_col)}$2:${get_column_letter(part_end_col)}${last_row}"
qty_range = f"${get_column_letter(qty_start_col)}$2:${get_column_letter(qty_end_col)}${last_row}"

formula = f'=SUMPRODUCT(({part_range}=$A2)*{qty_range})'

# Compute the same result literally, to provide a cached value for systems that do not recalculate formulas.
target = ws["A2"].value
computed_total = 0
for r in range(2, last_row + 1):
    for c in range(part_start_col, part_end_col + 1):
        if ws.cell(r, c).value == target:
            qty = ws.cell(r, c + 1).value
            if isinstance(qty, (int, float)):
                computed_total += qty

ws[answer_cell] = formula
wb.calculation.fullCalcOnLoad = True
wb.calculation.forceFullCalc = True
wb.calculation.calcMode = "auto"

# Save normally first.

# This keeps the requested formula visible while also making data_only readers see the computed result.

shutil.copy2(output_path, tmp_path)

ns = {"main": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main"}
ET.register_namespace("", ns["main"])

with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp_path, "r") as zin, zipfile.ZipFile(output_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:

            f_el = cell.find("main:f", ns)
